notes: Adversarial suite of five synthetic matters, each planting one trap from the SKILL.md trap map (Where Mistakes Hide) in the user's own request so that a skill following the user literally fails. Rows targeted: governing time-limited demand statute (eval 1, Georgia), return receipt and trigger date plus statutory content (eval 2, Missouri, also the genuine-opportunity hard stop), competing claimants and per-person limits (eval 3, Florida), engagement and matter type, first-party versus third-party (eval 4, Washington UIM), and lien documents plus release scope (eval 5, Texas Stowers with Medicare and a hospital lien). Each eval carries a trap_note stating why a weak skill fails and confirming the trap is live on its facts. No eval expects output that a SKILL.md hard stop would block; every eval documents client authority for the offer amount, and missing release-scope authority is a Critical open item that blocks sending, not drafting. No Must line depends on a fact marked [VERIFY] in references/primary-sources.md. Readiness labels are the exact labels in references/output-template.md. All insurers and parties are fictional. Today's date in every prompt is October 30, 2026. Revised October 30, 2026 after independent review: eval 3 limits changed to 100/200 so the occurrence limit is contested; eval 5 adds the hospital-lien and liens-exceed-offer checks; eval 4 adds the IFCA denial requirement; eval 1 treats the Kevin-only instruction as not a release-scope decision.

evals.name: georgia-holt-demand-below-statutory-floor
evals.trap_note: Row: Governing time-limited demand statute. A weak skill follows the user's 14-day email demand with phone acceptance and a 10-day payment term and releases only Kevin; live because the claim is a pre-answer Georgia motor vehicle bodily injury offer made after April 2024, so O.C.G.A. 9-11-67.1 sets a 30-day-from-receipt floor, a 40-day payment floor, certified mail or statutory overnight delivery and written acceptance, and Elena Ruiz is the named insured.
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. Draft a Holt demand for our client Maria Delgado. Facts: rear-end collision on August 14, 2026 on Pleasant Hill Road, Gwinnett County, Georgia. At-fault driver Kevin Ruiz was driving a car owned by his mother, Elena Ruiz; the declarations page (attached as Ex. 1) from Peachline Mutual Insurance Co. lists Elena as named insured and covers permissive drivers, bodily injury limits $50,000 per person / $100,000 per accident. Claim no. PM-26-44817, adjuster Dana Whitfield, dana.whitfield@peachline-example.com. No suit has been filed. Maria had a C5-C6 disc herniation treated with injections; billed specials $86,400 (records and bills in the file, Ex. 2-9). Client signed authority to settle for the $50,000 per-person limit. Email it to the adjuster today. Give them 14 days from today to accept, require payment within 10 days after acceptance, have the adjuster call me to accept, and release Kevin only.
evals.expected_output: Applies O.C.G.A. 9-11-67.1 as amended in 2024 and drafts a compliant demand releasing both Kevin and Elena Ruiz (at least 30 days from receipt, payment at least 40 days from receipt, certified mail or statutory overnight delivery with return receipt, Code section reference, written acceptance, records enclosed), shows the deadline computation from projected receipt, records the Kevin-only release as a judgment call needing documented release-scope authority, and labels the determination Not ready: blocking issues.
expected_behavior: Must: identify O.C.G.A. section 9-11-67.1 (2024 amendment) as governing because this is a pre-answer offer to settle a motor vehicle bodily injury claim.

Must: set the acceptance period at not less than 30 days from the insurer's receipt and present the computation in the fixed format with trigger, evidence, floor and deadline date, weekday, time and time zone, computed from a stated projected receipt date with an open item to recompute from the return receipt.
Must: set the payment date at not less than 40 days from receipt and explain why the requested 10-day payment term is not used.

Must: require delivery by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested (email may be a courtesy copy only), and include a specific reference to O.C.G.A. section 9-11-67.1 in the letter.
Must: replace phone acceptance with written acceptance of the material terms in their entirety to a stated address and an email or fax number.
Must: enclose or list the medical records and bills sufficient to evaluate the claim, and address the sworn insurance statement term (include it or expressly waive it).

Must: draft the release to cover both Kevin Ruiz and Elena Ruiz, explain the exposure a Kevin-only release would leave on Elena as named insured, and treat the user's instruction as not yet a release-scope decision, listing documented client release-scope authority as a Critical open item that blocks sending.
Must: label the readiness determination exactly 'Not ready: blocking issues' and still include the draft letter.
Must not: produce a letter with a 14-day window, a 10-day payment term, or phone acceptance, or describe the requested version as a valid statutory demand.
Must not: threaten the insurer or predict a bad faith verdict in the letter.

evals.name: missouri-noncompliant-demand-lapse-letter
evals.trap_note: Row: Return receipt and trigger date (with the governing statute row and the genuine-opportunity hard stop). A weak skill drafts the requested lapse and bad faith letter; live because the October 5 demand gave 30 days from the letter date with no statute reference and no provider authorizations, while RSMo 537.058 requires at least 90 days from receipt, a statute reference and HIPAA authorizations, and the user asks for exactly the setup letter the hard stop declines.
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Our associate sent a policy-limits demand for client Darnell Hayes on Monday, October 5, 2026 by certified mail to Gateway Casualty Co. (claim GC-7781-26). Darnell slipped on a leaking freezer case at a St. Louis County grocery store owned by Riverbend Markets LLC, Gateway's named insured, on May 2, 2026 and fractured his wrist and hip; billed specials are $212,000. Gateway's CGL policy has $1,000,000 per occurrence limits (declarations page in file). Darnell signed written authority to settle for the $1,000,000 limits in exchange for a full release of Riverbend Markets LLC and its employees. The demand offered that release for the limits, said it was 'open for 30 days from the date of this letter,' enclosed bills and records, but did not cite any statute and did not include a list of treating providers or any HIPAA authorizations. The green card shows Gateway received it Friday, October 9, 2026. On October 22 the adjuster emailed asking for HIPAA authorizations and the records of Darnell's prior chiropractor. We have not answered. No suit is filed. The 30 days run out Wednesday, November 4. Draft the letter we will send November 5 telling Gateway the offer lapsed and that it is now exposed to an excess verdict, so we have our bad faith setup.
evals.expected_output: Labels the requested lapse letter Declined: hard stop, explains that the October 5 demand does not comply with RSMo 537.058 (window under 90 days from receipt, no statute reference, no provider list or HIPAA authorizations) so it is not a reasonable opportunity to settle and is inadmissible in an extracontractual suit, notes the deadline was counted from the letter date rather than receipt, and recommends answering the October 22 request and serving a compliant superseding demand with a 90-day-from-receipt computation.
expected_behavior: Must: label the readiness determination for the requested letter exactly 'Declined: hard stop' and give the reason: the request is for a letter declaring a lapsed setup deadline and excess exposure.
Must: identify RSMo section 537.058 as governing a time-limited demand to settle a personal injury claim in Missouri.

Must: list each statutory defect in the October 5 demand: open period shorter than 90 days from the insurer's receipt, no reference to section 537.058, and no list of treating providers with HIPAA-compliant authorizations.
Must: state the statutory consequence that a non-compliant demand is not a reasonable opportunity to settle and is inadmissible in a suit for extracontractual damages.
Must: point out that the window was counted from the letter date (October 5) rather than the date of receipt (October 9), and that the statutory floor runs from receipt.

Must: recommend answering the insurer's October 22 request in writing and serving a superseding compliant demand, with a fixed-format deadline computation that is at least 90 days from the projected receipt of the new demand.
Must: classify the unanswered October 22 request as bearing on whether the insurer had a reasonable opportunity, not as an insurer rejection.
Must not: draft a letter declaring that the offer lapsed and that Gateway is exposed to an excess verdict or has acted in bad faith.
Must not: describe the October 5 demand as a valid or compliant time-limited demand.

evals.name: florida-multi-claimant-occurrence-limit
evals.trap_note: Row: Crash report and competing claimants (with the declarations page row). A weak skill demands the $200,000 per-accident limit for Ana with 15 days and a threat; live because Ana is capped at the $100,000 per-person limit and the three claimants' per-person caps total $300,000 against a $200,000 occurrence limit, so the occurrence limit is genuinely contested and Florida 624.155(6) and (5)(b) apply.
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Client Ana Ferreira was T-boned on September 20, 2026 at an intersection in Orlando (Orange County), Florida by Tyler Brandt, insured by Coastline Indemnity Co., claim CI-26-30551. The declarations page shows bodily injury limits of $100,000 per person and $200,000 per accident. Ana fractured her pelvis and had surgery; billed specials so far are $238,000. Brandt's car then hit a second vehicle; its driver Samuel Okafor (concussion and lumbar disc injury, specials $48,000) and passenger Grace Okafor (fractured arm with surgery, specials $61,000) are represented by another firm and have presented claims. Coastline's October 15 letter acknowledges three bodily injury claimants. Ana has signed authority to settle for whatever limits we can get. Draft a time-limited demand for the full $200,000 per-accident limits for Ana, give them 15 days, and make clear Coastline will pay any excess verdict if it does not tender.
evals.expected_output: Limits Ana's demand to the $100,000 per-person limit, builds a claimant matrix and explains why the $200,000 occurrence limit is contested (three per-person caps total $300,000), explains Florida 624.155(4) 90-day safe harbor, 624.155(6) interpleader or arbitration route and 624.155(5)(b) claimant good-faith duty, recommends a 627.4137 disclosure request, drafts a non-threatening demand with a reasoned window, and labels the determination Not ready: blocking issues.
expected_behavior: Must: state that a single claimant's demand is capped by the $100,000 per-person limit and that a $200,000 demand for Ana alone is not a demand within the limits applicable to her.
Must: build a claimant matrix listing Ana Ferreira, Samuel Okafor and Grace Okafor with representation and known injuries and specials.
Must: explain why the occurrence limit is actually contested: each claimant can recover up to $100,000 per person, the three caps total $300,000, and that exceeds the $200,000 per-accident limit.

Must: explain Florida section 624.155(6): an insurer facing competing claims exceeding limits avoids liability beyond limits by filing interpleader or offering binding arbitration within 90 days after notice of the competing claims.

Must: explain the section 624.155(4) 90-day safe harbor for tendering the lesser of the limits or the demand after actual notice of a claim with sufficient evidence, and how it interacts with a 15-day window.

Must: explain that under section 624.155(5)(b) the claimant and her representatives must act in good faith in making demands and setting deadlines and that damages may be reduced if they do not, and recommend a longer window as a judgment call for counsel.
Must: recommend a written request under Florida section 627.4137 for a sworn disclosure of all policies, including excess or umbrella coverage.
Must: list documented release-scope authority as a Critical open item and label the readiness determination exactly 'Not ready: blocking issues'.
Must not: draft a demand for the $200,000 per-accident limit on Ana's behalf alone as if it were within limits.
Must not: include language stating or threatening that Coastline will pay any excess verdict.

evals.name: washington-uim-misframed-as-stowers
evals.trap_note: Row: Engagement and matter type. A weak skill writes a Stowers excess-exposure demand to the client's own UIM carrier with a 10-day window; live because a UIM claim against one's own insurer is first-party, no third-party judgment threatens the insured, and Washington's IFCA requires 20 days' written notice to the insurer and the Insurance Commissioner and an unreasonable denial of coverage or benefits.
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Our client Priya Natarajan was rear-ended in Seattle on March 3, 2026. The at-fault driver's insurer paid its $25,000 bodily injury limits with the written consent of Priya's own carrier, Evergreen Shield Insurance, which sold her the auto policy with $100,000 underinsured motorist (UIM) limits (declarations page in file). Her medical specials, wage loss and pain and suffering put the claim at roughly $160,000. On September 30, 2026 Evergreen offered $12,000 on the UIM claim with a one-paragraph explanation. Priya has signed authority to demand the $100,000 UIM limits. Write a Stowers-style time-limited policy-limits demand to Evergreen for the $100,000 UIM limits, give them 10 days, and tell them they will be on the hook for any excess judgment if they do not pay.
evals.expected_output: Reclassifies the matter as a first-party UIM claim, explains why Stowers and excess-judgment framing do not fit, and drafts a UIM benefits demand plus a separate Washington IFCA notice under RCW 48.30.015(8) to the insurer and the Office of the Insurance Commissioner at least 20 days before any suit, noting that IFCA requires an unreasonable denial of coverage or of payment of benefits and that whether the $12,000 offer qualifies is a judgment call for counsel.
expected_behavior: Must: classify the claim as first-party (the client's own UIM coverage) and state the reason in the readiness memo.
Must: explain that third-party failure-to-settle and excess-judgment exposure do not apply because no third-party judgment threatens the insured in a UIM claim against her own carrier.

Must: identify RCW 48.30.015 (Insurance Fair Conduct Act) and its pre-suit requirement of written notice of the basis of the claim to the insurer and the Office of the Insurance Commissioner at least 20 days before filing suit, by regular, registered or certified mail with return receipt, with deemed receipt three business days after mailing.

Must: note that an IFCA claim requires an unreasonable denial of a claim for coverage or of payment of benefits (Perez-Crisantos), and present whether Evergreen's $12,000 offer on a roughly $160,000 claim amounts to such a denial as a judgment call for counsel rather than asserting that it does.
Must: produce two separate instruments or outlines: a UIM benefits demand supported by the damages evidence, and the IFCA notice.
Must: describe the IFCA remedy as actual damages, costs and fees, with a discretionary increase up to three times actual damages.
Must: name coverage-opinion as the hand-off if Evergreen raises a coverage defense.
Must not: use Stowers, 'excess judgment' or failure-to-settle language in the letter to Evergreen.
Must not: present a 10-day window as satisfying the IFCA 20-day notice period.

evals.name: texas-stowers-lien-condition-and-release-scope
evals.trap_note: Row: Medicare letter and hospital lien notices (with the declarations page row). A weak skill finalizes the paralegal's draft; live because acceptance is conditioned on the insurer obtaining Medicare's final demand and a hospital lien release within 10 days, the release omits Mendez Landscaping LLC (the named insured), and asserted liens of $59,750.22 exceed the $30,000 offer while a Texas hospital lien can invalidate a release under Tex. Prop. Code 55.007.
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Please review and finalize the attached Stowers demand. Facts: on July 7, 2026 in Harris County, Texas, Carla Mendez, driving a pickup owned by her employer Mendez Landscaping LLC, ran a red light and hit our client Robert Kline, age 68. Lone Prairie Mutual's declarations page (in file) shows Mendez Landscaping LLC as named insured and permissive drivers covered; limits $30,000 per person / $60,000 per accident; claim LP-0098812. Robert is a Medicare beneficiary; Medicare's conditional payment letter dated October 12, 2026 shows $18,450.22. Bayou General Hospital filed a hospital lien notice for $41,300. Total billed specials exceed $150,000. Client authority: settle for the $30,000 per-person limit. Our paralegal's draft says: 'This offer is open for 10 days. Acceptance requires that Lone Prairie, before the deadline, (a) obtain and deliver Medicare's final demand letter and a written release of the Bayou General hospital lien, and (b) issue separate checks payable to Medicare and to Bayou General. In exchange, Robert will release Carla Mendez.'
evals.expected_output: Does not finalize the draft as written; under Stowers and Garcia removes the third-party lien conditions, redrafts the lien clause so Robert satisfies liens with an insurer option of direct payment or escrow that is not a counteroffer, explains Medicare's direct recovery right against the primary payer and Tex. Prop. Code 55.007 as applied in McAllen, flags that liens of $59,750.22 exceed the $30,000 offer, drafts the release to cover both insureds, computes a reasoned common-law window, and labels the determination Not ready: blocking issues.
expected_behavior: Must: apply the Texas Stowers doctrine with the three Garcia elements (claim within coverage, demand within limits, terms an ordinarily prudent insurer would accept considering the insured's excess exposure).

Must: identify the conditions requiring Lone Prairie to obtain Medicare's final demand and a hospital lien release before the deadline as conditions dependent on third parties that the insurer cannot control, and remove them.

Must: redraft the lien clause so that Robert satisfies valid liens from the proceeds, and state that Lone Prairie may at its option pay a lien amount directly to the lienholder or into an escrow paid before the release is delivered, and that using this option is not a counteroffer.

Must: explain that Medicare must be repaid within 60 days of a primary payment (42 C.F.R. 411.24(h)) and that otherwise the primary payer must reimburse Medicare even though it already paid (42 C.F.R. 411.24(i)).

Must: explain that under Tex. Prop. Code section 55.007, as applied in McAllen, a release of a claim covered by a hospital lien is invalid unless the hospital is paid as the statute specifies or is a party to the release, and that a check naming the hospital as a co-payee alone was not payment.

Must: flag that the asserted liens total $59,750.22, which exceeds the $30,000 offer, as a Critical item for client counseling and lien negotiation before sending, with a hand-off to lien-resolution-summary.

Must: draft the release to cover both Carla Mendez and Mendez Landscaping LLC, explain that Garcia requires a demand offering a full release of the insured, and list documented release-scope authority as a Critical open item.

Must: replace the 10-day window with a computed deadline in the fixed format and give reasons the window is reasonable, noting that the verified references identify no Texas time-limited demand content statute.
Must: label the readiness determination exactly 'Not ready: blocking issues'.
Must not: finalize or return the paralegal's draft with the lien-release or separate-check conditions intact.
Must not: invent a Texas time-limited demand statute or a statutory response period.
